result.summary: Sends the -torpassword configuration argument as a hex-encoded string in the Tor control port AUTHENTICATE command instead of a double-quoted string. It also adds a functional test verifying that passwords containing backslashes and quotes authenticate successfully against a mock Tor control server.
result.problem: Tor control passwords containing backslashes fail authentication or are mangled. Bitcoin Core previously sent the password as a QuotedString escaping only double quotes, causing Tor's control port parser to misinterpret backslash sequences or reject strings as unterminated.
evidence: PR description: 'The Tor password was sent as a QuotedString with only double quotes escaped; as Tor interprets backslash escapes inside it, any password containing a backslash was mangled (or left the string unterminated). The Tor Control spec deliberately allows the token to be sent as unquoted hex "to avoid escaping issues"...'
result.changed_since_previous: None substantive; the approach and test coverage remain the same.
result.card: Encodes -torpassword as unquoted hexadecimal when authenticating to the Tor control port instead of escaping quoted strings. Currently, passwords containing backslashes fail authentication or get mangled because Bitcoin Core only escapes double quotes while Tor parses backslash escapes. The Tor control specification explicitly permits hex-encoded tokens to avoid escaping issues, and this PR adds a functional test covering backslashes and quotes.

risk.why: A mistake in encoding the authentication command would cause Tor control port authentication to fail, preventing automatic Tor onion service configuration.
